entries.title: Proverbs 18:1
segments: Having separated himself; from society, that he may give himself to study.  But many render this verse thus: he who separateth himself from his fellow-men, seeketh after his own desire; he opposeth himself to all wisdom.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:2
segments: They who have least wisdom are most fond of uttering their opinions.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:3
segments:
Cometh; into power and influence. 
 
  Contempt, and with ignominy reproach; contempt and reproach heaped by him upon his fellow-man. 
 
When the wicked come into power they fill society with abuse and contumely.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:4
segments:
A man's mouth; that is, a wise man's mouth. 
 
  Well-spring of wisdom; which gushes forth from his heart, and is inexhaustible.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:5
segments: To overthrow; in order to overthrow.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:6
segments:
Calleth for strokes; provokes men to inflict stripes upon him. 
 
The words of a foolish man are as calamitous to himself as to others. They fill society with contentions, and bring upon him condign punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:8
segments: Into the innermost parts of the belly; inflicting mortal wounds.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:9
segments: Sloth and prodigality lead to the same end, want and misery.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:11
segments: It is natural to fallen man to trust in uncertain riches, rather than in the living God.  This makes the salvation of the rich exceedingly difficult--harder than for a camel to go through the eye of a needle.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:12
segments: A man's spirit is a sure indication of the lot that awaits him: if he be humble, honor; if haughty, ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:13
segments:
Answereth a matter; gives his opinion on a matter. 
 
It is a good rule not to express an opinion till we have had a full opportunity to hear both sides.  He who pursues the opposite course proclaims his folly, and brings upon himself perpetual mortification.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:14
segments:
The spirit of a man--a wounded spirit; the meaning is, that a courageous spirit will enable a man to bear up under the pressure of grief and pain; but a broken and desponding spirit, that has lost the power of endurance, is an intolerable evil. 
 
By courage and faith all evils are made tolerable.  A pusillanimous spirit, that faints at the approach of trouble, is as distressing as it is sinful.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:17
segments:
First in his own cause; first in telling his own story. 
 
  His neighbor; his antagonist.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:21
segments: They that love it shall eat the fruit thereof; they that will exercise the gift of speech must reap the consequences, be they good or evil.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:22
segments: God has ordained the marriage relation for the purity, comfort, and usefulness of man.  Notwithstanding all the evils which human depravity has introduced into it, it is, in general, better than to be alone; and he who finds a wise and virtuous wife, receives from God the richest earthly blessing.

entries.title: Proverbs 18:23
segments: The tendency of wealth to foster pride and haughtiness of spirit, is great.  To be rich, and at the same time truly humble, is the fruit of divine grace.
